title: CDL inspection and maintenance practice questions
description: Free CDL inspection and maintenance practice questions on 49 CFR Part 396. Every answer is explained and linked to the section it comes from.

questions.question: Under 49 CFR 396.3(a), who must systematically inspect, repair, and maintain (or cause this to be done for) all motor vehicles subject to its control?

options.A: Each driver, for the vehicle the driver is assigned
options.B: Every motor carrier
options.C: The State agency that registered the vehicle
options.D: The vehicle manufacturer, during the warranty period

questions.explanation: "Every motor carrier and intermodal equipment provider must systematically inspect, repair, and maintain, or cause to be systematically inspected, repaired, and maintained, all motor vehicles and intermodal equipment subject to its control."

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 396.3, Inspection, repair, and maintenance (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: Every motor carrier and intermodal equipment provider must systematically inspect, repair, and maintain, or cause to be systematically inspected, repaired, and maintained, all motor vehicles and intermodal equipment subject to its control.

questions.question: What inspection interval does 396.3(a)(2) set for pushout windows, emergency doors, and emergency door marking lights in buses?

options.A: At least every 12 months
options.B: At least every 180 days
options.C: At least every 120 days
options.D: At least every 90 days

questions.explanation: Under 396.3(a)(2), these bus items "shall be inspected at least every 90 days."

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 396.3, Inspection, repair, and maintenance (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: Pushout windows, emergency doors, and emergency door marking lights in buses shall be inspected at least every 90 days.

questions.question: What does 396.5 require every motor carrier to ensure about each motor vehicle subject to its control?

options.A: That it is properly lubricated and free of oil and grease leaks
options.B: That its engine oil is changed at a mileage set in the rule
options.C: That the driver logs each lubrication in the daily report
options.D: That only the manufacturer's brand of lubricant is used

questions.explanation: Every motor carrier "shall ensure that each motor vehicle subject to its control is" "Properly lubricated" and "Free of oil and grease leaks."

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 396.5, Lubrication (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: Every motor carrier shall ensure that each motor vehicle subject to its control is— (a) Properly lubricated; and (b) Free of oil and grease leaks.

questions.question: Under 396.7(b), how far may a motor vehicle discovered to be in an unsafe condition while being operated on the highway be continued in operation?

options.A: To the end of the driver's current shift
options.B: To the motor carrier's home terminal
options.C: Only to the nearest place where repairs can safely be effected
options.D: To any destination within the same State

questions.explanation: Such a vehicle "may be continued in operation only to the nearest place where repairs can safely be effected," and only if "it is less hazardous to the public than to permit the vehicle to remain on the highway."

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 396.7, Unsafe operations forbidden (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: Any motor vehicle discovered to be in an unsafe condition while being operated on the highway may be continued in operation only to the nearest place where repairs can safely be effected. Such operation shall be conducted only if it is less hazardous to the public than to permit the vehicle to remain on the highway.

questions.question: What retention period does 396.3(c) set for the maintenance records required by 396.3?

options.A: 1 year where the vehicle is housed or maintained, and 6 months after the vehicle leaves the motor carrier's control
options.B: 3 months from the date of each repair
options.C: 30 days after the vehicle leaves the motor carrier's control
options.D: Only until the vehicle's next periodic inspection

questions.explanation: The records "shall be retained where the vehicle is either housed or maintained for a period of 1 year and for 6 months after the motor vehicle leaves the motor carrier's control."

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 396.3, Inspection, repair, and maintenance (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: The records required by this section shall be retained where the vehicle is either housed or maintained for a period of 1 year and for 6 months after the motor vehicle leaves the motor carrier's control.

questions.question: Which kind of motor carrier does 396.3(b) except from the requirement to maintain records for each motor vehicle it controls?

options.A: A for-hire motor carrier of property
options.B: A private motor carrier of passengers (nonbusiness)
options.C: A motor carrier with fewer than 10 vehicles
options.D: A motor carrier that leases all of its vehicles

questions.explanation: "Motor carriers, except for a private motor carrier of passengers (nonbusiness), must maintain, or cause to be maintained, records for each motor vehicle they control for 30 consecutive days."

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 396.3, Inspection, repair, and maintenance (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: Motor carriers, except for a private motor carrier of passengers (nonbusiness), must maintain, or cause to be maintained, records for each motor vehicle they control for 30 consecutive days.

questions.question: Under 396.9(c)(2), how may a vehicle marked "out-of-service" be towed away before the required repairs are completed?

options.A: By any truck using a tow bar
options.B: In combination behind another vehicle of the same motor carrier
options.C: Only after the driver removes the out-of-service sticker
options.D: By means of a vehicle using a crane or hoist

questions.explanation: "Operate" includes towing, "except that vehicles or intermodal equipment marked “out-of-service” may be towed away by means of a vehicle using a crane or hoist."

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 396.9, Inspection of motor vehicles and intermodal equipment in operation (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: The term operate as used in this section shall include towing the vehicle or intermodal equipment, except that vehicles or intermodal equipment marked “out-of-service” may be towed away by means of a vehicle using a crane or hoist.

questions.question: What deadline does 396.9(d)(3) set for the motor carrier to certify that all violations noted on a roadside inspection report have been corrected?

options.A: 30 days following the date of the inspection
options.B: 60 days following the date of the inspection
options.C: 15 days following the date of the inspection
options.D: 90 days following the date of the inspection

questions.explanation: "Within 15 days following the date of the inspection, the motor carrier or intermodal equipment provider shall" "Certify that all violations noted have been corrected."

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 396.9, Inspection of motor vehicles and intermodal equipment in operation (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: Within 15 days following the date of the inspection, the motor carrier or intermodal equipment provider shall— (i) Certify that all violations noted have been corrected

questions.question: Under 396.9(c)(3), when may a person remove the "Out-of-Service Vehicle" sticker from a motor vehicle?

options.A: As soon as the vehicle reaches the next terminal
options.B: 24 hours after the inspection
options.C: When the motor carrier's dispatcher approves
options.D: Not before all repairs required by the "out-of-service notice" are completed

questions.explanation: "No person shall remove the “Out-of-Service Vehicle” sticker from any motor vehicle or intermodal equipment prior to completion of all repairs required by the “out-of-service notice.”"

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 396.9, Inspection of motor vehicles and intermodal equipment in operation (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: No person shall remove the “Out-of-Service Vehicle” sticker from any motor vehicle or intermodal equipment prior to completion of all repairs required by the “out-of-service notice.”

questions.question: Under 396.9(d)(1), what must a driver who receives an inspection report do if the driver is not scheduled to arrive at a terminal or facility of the motor carrier operating the vehicle within 24 hours?

options.A: Immediately mail, fax, or otherwise transmit the report to the motor carrier
options.B: Keep the report until the next scheduled arrival at a terminal
options.C: Send the report to FMCSA instead of the motor carrier
options.D: Give the report to the next State inspector met on the route

questions.explanation: In that case "the driver shall immediately mail, fax, or otherwise transmit the report to the motor carrier and intermodal equipment provider."

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 396.9, Inspection of motor vehicles and intermodal equipment in operation (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: If the driver is not scheduled to arrive at a terminal or facility of the motor carrier operating the vehicle or at a facility of the intermodal equipment provider within 24 hours, the driver shall immediately mail, fax, or otherwise transmit the report to the motor carrier and intermodal equipment provider.

questions.question: Under 396.11(a)(1), when does a driver prepare the written driver vehicle inspection report on each vehicle operated?

options.A: Before the start of each trip
options.B: Once at the end of each week
options.C: At the completion of each day's work
options.D: Only after a roadside inspection

questions.explanation: "Every driver shall prepare a report in writing at the completion of each day's work on each vehicle operated."

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 396.11, Driver vehicle inspection report(s) (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: Every motor carrier shall require its drivers to report, and every driver shall prepare a report in writing at the completion of each day's work on each vehicle operated, except for intermodal equipment tendered by an intermodal equipment provider.

questions.question: What retention period does 396.25(e) set for the evidence of a brake inspector's qualifications?

options.A: For 30 days after the brake inspector is hired
options.B: For the period the brake inspector is employed in that capacity and for one year thereafter
options.C: Until the brake inspector's next CDL renewal
options.D: For 90 days after each brake inspection

questions.explanation: "The evidence must be maintained for the period during which the brake inspector is employed in that capacity and for one year thereafter."

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 396.25, Qualifications of brake inspectors (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: The evidence must be maintained for the period during which the brake inspector is employed in that capacity and for one year thereafter.

questions.question: What does 396.11(a)(2)(i) say about preparing a driver vehicle inspection report when no defect or deficiency is discovered by or reported to the driver?

options.A: Drivers are not required to prepare a report
options.B: The driver must still prepare a report marked "no defects"
options.C: The driver must report by telephone instead of in writing
options.D: The motor carrier must prepare the report for the driver

questions.explanation: The rule states: "Drivers are not required to prepare a report if no defect or deficiency is discovered by or reported to the driver."

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 396.11, Driver vehicle inspection report(s) (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: Drivers are not required to prepare a report if no defect or deficiency is discovered by or reported to the driver.

questions.question: On a two-driver operation, how many drivers need to sign the driver vehicle inspection report under 396.11(a)(2)(ii)?

options.A: Both drivers, in every case
options.B: Neither driver; the motor carrier signs it
options.C: The driver who drove the most hours, plus a carrier official
options.D: Only one, provided both drivers agree as to the defects or deficiencies identified

questions.explanation: "On two-driver operations, only one driver needs to sign the driver vehicle inspection report, provided both drivers agree as to the defects or deficiencies identified."

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 396.11, Driver vehicle inspection report(s) (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: The driver must sign the report. On two-driver operations, only one driver needs to sign the driver vehicle inspection report, provided both drivers agree as to the defects or deficiencies identified.

questions.question: What retention period does 396.11(a)(4) set for the driver vehicle inspection report, the certification of repairs, and the certification of the driver's review?

options.A: 24 hours from the end of the trip
options.B: Three months from the date the written report was prepared
options.C: 30 days from the date the written report was prepared
options.D: 7 days from the date the written report was prepared

questions.explanation: "Every motor carrier shall maintain the driver vehicle inspection report, the certification of repairs, and the certification of the driver's review for three months from the date the written report was prepared."

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 396.11, Driver vehicle inspection report(s) (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: Every motor carrier shall maintain the driver vehicle inspection report, the certification of repairs, and the certification of the driver's review for three months from the date the written report was prepared.

questions.question: What minimum total of training or experience does 396.19(a)(3)(ii) set for an individual qualifying that way to perform annual inspections?

options.A: 30 days
options.B: 90 days
options.C: 1 year
options.D: 6 months

questions.explanation: One option is to "Have a combination of training or experience totaling at least 1 year."

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 396.19, Inspector qualifications (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: Have a combination of training or experience totaling at least 1 year.

questions.question: Under 396.13(a), what must the driver be satisfied of before driving a motor vehicle?

options.A: That the motor carrier has approved the trip in writing
options.B: That the motor vehicle is in safe operating condition
options.C: That the vehicle has been washed and fueled
options.D: That a State inspector has checked the vehicle that day

questions.explanation: "Before driving a motor vehicle, the driver shall: (a) Be satisfied that the motor vehicle is in safe operating condition".

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 396.13, Driver inspection (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: Before driving a motor vehicle, the driver shall: (a) Be satisfied that the motor vehicle is in safe operating condition;

questions.question: What inspection period does 396.17(c) set before a motor carrier may use a commercial motor vehicle, for each component in Appendix A (with documentation on the vehicle)?

options.A: At least once during the preceding 12 months
options.B: At least once during the preceding 24 months
options.C: At least once during the preceding 36 months
options.D: Only once, when the vehicle is first placed in service

questions.explanation: Each component must have "passed an inspection in accordance with the terms of this section at least once during the preceding 12 months and documentation of such inspection is on the vehicle."

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 396.17, Periodic inspection (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: A motor carrier must not use a commercial motor vehicle, and an intermodal equipment provider must not tender equipment to a motor carrier for interchange, unless each component identified in appendix A to this part has passed an inspection in accordance with the terms of this section at least once during the preceding 12 months and documentation of such inspection is on the vehicle.

questions.question: Under 396.17(a), which vehicles of a tractor semitrailer, full trailer combination must each be inspected?

options.A: Only the tractor
options.B: Only the tractor and the semitrailer
options.C: The tractor, the semitrailer, and the full trailer (including the converter dolly if so equipped)
options.D: Only the unit with the highest mileage

questions.explanation: "For example, for a tractor semitrailer, full trailer combination, the tractor, semitrailer, and the full trailer (including the converter dolly if so equipped) must each be inspected."

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 396.17, Periodic inspection (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: The term commercial motor vehicle includes each vehicle in a combination vehicle. For example, for a tractor semitrailer, full trailer combination, the tractor, semitrailer, and the full trailer (including the converter dolly if so equipped) must each be inspected.

questions.question: What retention period does 396.21(b)(1) set for the original or a copy of the periodic inspection report?

options.A: 3 months from the date of the inspection report
options.B: 6 months from the date of the inspection report
options.C: 30 days from the date of the inspection report
options.D: Fourteen months from the date of the inspection report

questions.explanation: The report "shall be retained by the motor carrier, intermodal equipment provider, or other entity that is responsible for the inspection for a period of fourteen months from the date of the inspection report."

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 396.21, Periodic inspection recordkeeping requirements (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: The original or a copy of the inspection report shall be retained by the motor carrier, intermodal equipment provider, or other entity that is responsible for the inspection for a period of fourteen months from the date of the inspection report.
